newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower after ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called a bit lower after ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly lower Thursday after a weaker ACCESS session, market sources said.
Following June's expiration 1.7 cents lower at $2.346 per million British thermal units, July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.29 to $2.31.
July settled to the downside Wednesday at $2.316, and then extended those losses on ACCESS to last trade 2.6 cents lower at $2.29.
Technically, traders said July support was at $2.28 and $2.25. Resistance was seen at $2.37-2.38 and then at the contract high of $2.44.

In Wednesday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed a few cents to the high-$2.20s for next-day delivery, while June gas on the same pipes was quoted in the low-$2.30s. May Midcon gas gained a similar amount to the low-teens, with June around $2.15. New York city gate gas for May was steady to up slightly near $2.50.
Cooler-than-normal weather continued throughout most of the upper Midwest, while temperature highs over 100 degrees F baked Arizona, according to Weather Services Corp.
Keeping supply tight was news that the 1,221 megawatt Palo Verde 1 nuclear unit was still off line despite earlier reports that it would likely restart late Wednesday.
Meanwhile, Texas Utilities' 1,150 MW Comanche Peak unit was increasing power after operating at a reduced rate.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 76 bcf, in line with expectations, and were still 212 bcf, or 24 percent, over year-ago levels. Eastern storage, which gained 47 bcf last week, remained 107 bcf, or 26 percent, above a year ago.
